newsitem.title: USA: Madonna turns out for star-studded Evita premiere.
newsitem.headline: Madonna turns out for star-studded Evita premiere.

text.p: Pop singer Madonna and other Hollywood stars were out in force on Saturday night for the long-awaited world premiere of "Evita", a movie musical about Eva Peron's rise to power in Argentina.
"I feel like Cinderella," said a teary-eyed Madonna as she strode down the red carpet in front of thousands of screaming fans at the Shrine Auditorium.

"Evita", which opens on Christmas Day, is a screen opera about the life of Eva Peron, the daughter of a poor farmer who became the wife of Argentina's President Juan Peron, played by Jonathan Pryce, and wielded power in her own right.

Director Alan Parker and other cast members said the pop diva, who is no stranger to scandal, was perfectly cast to play Evita, who was considered a saint by the working class but was often maligned by members of the ruling class.

"She's extraordinarily professional and hard-working," director Alan Parker said of Madonna as he arrived at the festive premiere. "She was always brilliantly prepared and very charismatic. It's very easy to work with her."
Madonna, wearing a rose-coloured Givenchy dress with a nipped-in waist, was one of several celebrities who turned out for the event wearing outfits inspired by Eva Peron's era.
"I love the style, the padded shoulders. It's the power woman look," said actress Tippi Hedren.

While fashion designers are already betting that the holiday season's most-anticipated movie will draw floods of women to the stores in search of Evita-style clothes, many celebrities are also hoping that the film will breathe new life into the movie musical of yesteryear.
"Evita", which is woven around the songs of the popular Broadway musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice, includes no spoken dialogue.
"I really hope that musicals become popular again. I loved all those Fred Astaire films," said actress Marisa Tomei who turned out for the premiere.

Tony-award winning actress Glenn Close, currently starring in the popular "101 Dalmations", said, "It's one of the great musicals. The music is just mind-boggling, very emotional, very beautiful and it's a wonderful coming together of the character and the musical," she said.
The film's producers hope the star-studded cast, which also includes heart-throb Antonio Banderas as the film's cynical Everyman narrator, will be the recipe for a box-office smash.

Yet, with the unusual operatic format, distributor Walt Disney Co decided to take no chances and ran full-page advertisements announcing advance ticket sales for the epic musical as early as three months ago.
Indeed, the movie's premiere was considerably more hyped than most premieres in Tinsel Town, according to several celebrities.
"This is a circus!" said Banderas, smiling and standing close to his wife, actress Melanie Griffith, before they entered the auditorium.
